judged_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — P2 confidence 100 advisory — Cascading-dependency coupling: when the configured sync service is unavailable, the synchronous `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` becomes one shared failure boundary for every expired user-owned Google, HubSpot, Lark, Office 365, Teams, and Webex credential and calendar/video operations fail or continue with stale auth; the strongest counterargument is that the parent service is the authoritative token owner, but the issue survives because one global endpoint couples unrelated providers and provider fallback exists only when configuration is absent rather than when the dependency fails.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies an architectural concern in the new refreshOAuthTokens.ts function. Looking at the diff, when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are configured, ALL OAuth token refreshes (Google, HubSpot, Lark, Office365, Teams, Webex, Zoom, Zoho) route through a single endpoint. If that endpoint fails, there's no fallback to the original refresh function - the code either uses the sync endpoint OR the original function, not both with fallback. This is a legitimate architectural concern about coupling multiple providers to a single point of failure. However, this is by design for self-hosters integrating Cal.com into their applications, so it's an important design consideration rather than a bug.
